extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale robotic failure question-answering dataset covering tasks of varying complexity in simulated and real-world environments, with diverse backgrounds and camera viewpoints. It contains 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 tasks and 53 scenes for failure analysis and correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by collecting simulated robotic task trajectories for 14 tasks in ManiSkill with augmented objects and scenes, generating failures by replacing expert policies with erroneous trajectory code at selected substages, recording each failure video with descriptive text, manually cleaning misaligned trajectories, and collecting real-world data for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of robotic failure videos and successful trajectories from simulation and real-world executions, each accompanied by descriptive text including the failure substage, taxonomy, detailed explanation, and for some failures the perturbed end-effector pose.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data were annotated into video-based QA samples for eight question types using five question templates per type. For five question types, reference answers were directly extracted from textual descriptions. For three question types (failure explanation, high-level correction, low-level correction), prompts constructed from description files and paired with videos were sent to GPT-4o to generate answers, and all GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was ensured by manual review and correction of all GPT-4o-generated outputs.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o was used to annotate/generate reference answers for failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction questions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased toward robotic failure scenarios and is designed around six predefined failure categories, with diversity introduced through varied tasks, scenes, backgrounds, and camera viewpoints.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current system integration is not seamless, correction delivery is not yet natural or automated, and the work applies the model only to VLA models rather than broader policy architectures such as hierarchical policies.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper suggests the dataset and model can improve robotic failure recovery and increase success rates in real-world robotic control tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking multimodal models for robotic failure video understanding, including task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction, and for integration as an external critic in VLA control pipelines.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The model and dataset are publicly available.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Simulation data were augmented with additional objects and scenes to increase diversity, and failure data were generated by replacing the expert policy with code that produces erroneous trajectories at selected substages.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The collected data were manually cleaned to remove trajectories that did not match their textual descriptions, retaining about 75% of the data.
